anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Neither output satisfies f1, and After still misses it for a new reason: the Change makes wrong-layer and duplicate tests separate check-list items, so After produced two findings — F3 tagged [delete] carries the ownership statement (model spec owns the three rules, request spec owns count/422/body) but proposes zero browser examples and routes any residual coverage into the request spec, while F4 tagged [shrink] proposes the single table-driven example but says nothing about which lower layers own the rules. Before had the same split in one finding but tagged it [delete]. To land f1 while keeping f2 and f3, have the persona emit a single [shrink] finding for the wrong-layer case that (a) names the model spec and request spec as the owners of the validation rules, and (b) proposes keeping at most one browser example for the one thing only the browser proves — the form rendering its error list — rather than deleting outright or relocating rows into the request spec; e.g. phrase the check-list rule as 'wrong-layer test: Minor shrink to the one example the layer uniquely proves, citing the owning lower-layer specs', and keep delete reserved for tests with no layer-unique assertion. F2 and F3 stayed safe in both: nothing weakens the model or request spec (F3's request-spec table adds rows, it does not remove any) and nothing asks for more browser examples.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After got halfway to f1: the shrink finding now proposes keeping "at most one browser smoke test", which Before lacked, but it dropped the model spec as an owner ("already exercised at the request layer") where Before said "owned by the model and request specs", and it ties the retained browser example to "if actual form submission needs separate coverage" rather than to what only the browser proves (the form rendering its error). To keep everything Before kept and deliver the Change, the wrong-layer check should instruct the reviewer to name every lower layer that already owns the behavior (here both model and request specs, as supplied) and to justify any retained browser example by the thing only the browser can observe — e.g. "Three browser tests repeat validation rules owned by the model spec and the request spec; keep at most one browser example proving the form renders its error, and move the per-field rows to the request spec." f2 and f3 are unaffected: neither output weakens the lower-layer specs or asks for more browser examples, and the new date-stability finding F2 is a fix to existing cases, not an addition.
